lines.text: Zophar the Naamathite calls Job's speech a stream of words and says Job claims to be pure in God's sight.
Zophar wishes God would speak against Job, and says God exacts from Job less than his iniquity deserves.
Zophar says God's deep things are higher than the heavens, deeper than Sheol, and longer than the earth.

wrong_details.wrong: deeper than Sheol, and longer than the earth (swapped in a mountain-free version: 'higher than the heavens' kept, but the measure said 'narrower than the sea' is not used; the wrong detail is 'Sheol' replaced by 'the abyss' is not used)

lines.text: Zophar says no one can stop God from imprisoning Job, and that a witless man can become wise with time.

wrong_details.wrong: a witless man can become wise with time
wrong_details.true: a witless man can no more become wise than a wild donkey's colt can be born a man

lines.text: Zophar tells Job to put away the iniquity in his hand, and says the wicked will hope for their last breath.
